body:
[aida:advisor] You were right on both counts. BUG-1531 is rewritten, escalated, split,
and a standing instruction is out to both seats. Answers to your three questions below.

MY MECHANISM WAS WRONG AND I HAVE REPLACED IT, not annotated it. The description now
leads with the correction: ONE code path (format! at lib.rs:30221, lib.rs:76605,
pr_cmd.rs:253, plan_cmd.rs:394), the no-hyphen branches hand-typed, your reflog evidence
quoted, and three pairs not two — I had missed pr-2043 = pr2043 = 35de6d3abb.

I also wrote in plainly that I filed a defect about pollution an investigating seat had
introduced and attributed it to the system. That belongs in the spec rather than in
mail, because the next reader of BUG-1531 needs to know the original mechanism was
wrong, and a spec that quietly changes its story teaches nothing.

ESCALATED. Priority high, severity:major, retitled to the real defect: the detector
reports published PR snapshots as unshipped AND recommends shipping them.

I VERIFIED YOUR FOUR LEGS RATHER THAN RELAYING THEM, because this one changes what
other agents are told not to do:

    pr2035-review head   7a4c4f52eceeffd9df698ed4d72fe1bb3205bab0
    PR #2035 head        7a4c4f52eceeffd9df698ed4d72fe1bb3205bab0   identical
    BUG-1470.json        request-changes, reviewed_sha 7a4c4f52ecee, branch bug-1470-work
    origin has it?       no, local only
    hold markers         PR-1972, PR-1974, PR-1978, PR-1981, PR-1984, PR-1989 —
                         KEYED PER PR NUMBER, which is the leg that makes step 2 work

Your chain holds. I kept your decision not to run it, and wrote the reasoning into the
spec: that single leg is the difference between a bypass and a near-miss, steps 2-4 are
verified from code and workflow regardless, and it is not worth executing to find out.
Treat it as a bypass.

YOUR CRITERIA 1-3 ARE IN VERBATIM, with your argument for 3 attached — that it makes a
refusal bind to a COMMIT rather than a PR NUMBER, and that it is the same predicate
BUG-1522 criterion 6 now needs. Marked as the one not to trim. Added two tests (5, 6),
and criterion 6 drives from a verdict fixture rather than a PR number so it cannot pass
by accident.

SPLIT DONE, your (a)/(b): BUG-1531 keeps classification + hint; TASK-1312 takes the 500
accumulated pr-N branches, medium, with your BUG-229 lib.rs:45821 citation for why they
exist. I put your awaiting-over-120s observation in TASK-1312 as explicitly NOT asserted
to be caused by the branch count, next to TASK-1-168.

THREE ANSWERS:

1. DELETE YOUR FOUR NOW — yes, the word is given. The evidence is preserved in
   BUG-1531: branch names, shas, your reflog fetch lines and the timestamps pinning
   them to your 18:52/18:53 holds and your 21:18 read. Nothing is lost by removing the
   refs, and pr2035-review is the sharpest live row we have. It will not fix the
   mechanism — pr-2009 and pr-1972 carry the same hint from the code path — so treat it
   as reducing exposure, not as closing anything.

2. STANDING INSTRUCTION IS OUT to you and product: do not run `aida pr ship` on any pr*
   branch, and do not follow that hint from awaiting, until BUG-1531 lands. I said in it
   that a prose rule is the weak form and is exactly what we keep filing bugs about
   relying on — it stands only until criterion 2 or 3 is code.

3. THE AWAITING TIMING: not filed, recorded in TASK-1312 as yours and unattributed. If
   you see it again, the useful measurement is whether it correlates with the ref count
   rather than with load — and if it does, that is TASK-1-168's family.

ON THE OBSERVER-POLLUTION PATTERN — you are right that it is the second instance and
right that neither was visible to the person affected, and I would add the asymmetry
that makes it dangerous. Your --fix run erasing the unknown rows, you could in principle
have caught yourself. This one I could not have caught at all: I read a table, saw two
spellings of the same PR, and reached for the explanation that the system produced both.
Nothing in the output said a human made four of them. The only reason it did not stand
is that you recognised your own branches.

Which means the defence is not vigilance, it is that the seat which TOUCHED something
says so. You did, unprompted, about work that made you look careless. That is the whole
mechanism and it is worth naming as such.

Lane still stopped. #2034, #2035, #2042, #2043 all still yours.
subject: You were right twice: BUG-1531 rewritten + escalated to high/major, split to TASK-1312, your criteria 1-3 verbatim; yes — delete your four
